audit.whatIsWrong: Six of the seven chart rows contradict their own whys[] text.
audit.why: The whys[] read Even, Even, Even, Teemo, Even, Teemo, Teemo — which is exactly the packet chart (Skill, Skill, Skill, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Teemo) over 1802 games at 48.95%. The side rows read Teemo, Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Skill, Teemo instead.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2 and 4 to Skill, rows 3 and 5 to Teemo, as matched full/content pairs with ratings and reasons.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown anywhere, and the level-6 line does not say why your ultimate is only a partial answer here.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at 680 range — it does not scale down, so the gap is the same all game and is trackable. Noxious Trap is charge-based on a 0.25s throw at 600/750/900 range and mushrooms bounce off other mushrooms for extra reach. Undying Rage 120/100/80. Teemo's real spikes are item-driven blind uptime, not levels.
audit.corrected: The flat 7s written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and the phase reasons; the mushroom bounce into dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The blind is described only as 'blinds your crit-autos'. That understates it by half, and Move Quick is called a passive when it is both.
audit.why: Tryndamere's Fury comes from attacks, critical strikes and killing blows, and Bloodlust consumes Fury to heal. A blind stops the autos, which stops the Fury, which leaves Bloodlust with nothing to convert — the blind removes your damage AND your sustain from one cast. Riot's Move Quick text: the passive speed lasts 'until he is struck by an enemy champion or turret', while the active sprint 'isn't stopped by being struck' — so landing one auto strips the passive but not the active.
audit.corrected: The double starve written into report[5].t, phases[1].why and mid; Move Quick named to its slot.

audit.why: Mercury's Treads and a sweeper are already prescribed, which fits Toxic Shot's on-hit magic damage and Guerrilla Warfare's brush invisibility. Armour would read the trade wrong, and the page does not recommend it.

edits.before: Spin up fury on the wave before contesting anything. Identify how Teemo contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Spin up fury on the wave — Blinding Dart is 7s at rank 1, so trade inside the gap and never walk in while it is up.

edits.before: E lets you spin in and out of exchanges on your terms. Only take the trade when Teemo's Blinding Dart is down.
edits.after: Blinding Dart starves you twice: no autos means no Fury, so Bloodlust has nothing left to convert.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Teemo must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but his blind is the gate. Keep the wave near your side so he has to step into your 650 Spinning Slash.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Blinding Dart's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His window: a well-timed Blinding Dart cancels your whole all-in and Move Quick kites the follow-up. Bait the dart first.

edits.before: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds — dives and coin-flip all-ins become yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Teemo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds — a real kill window — but Noxious Trap slows and poisons the retreat, so path around the obvious mushroom spots.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Blinding Dart's cooldown.
edits.after: His spike: item power lifts his blind uptime and poke, so only commit inside the 7s gap.

edits.before: Level 3-5 Teemo takes over: a well-timed Blinding Dart cancels your entire all-in and his movespeed lets him kite the follow-up, so you have to bait the blind first. Level 6 you get a small window with Undying Rage, but his shrooms punish sloppy dives.
edits.after: Level 3-5 Teemo takes over: a well-timed Blinding Dart cancels your all-in — no autos means no Fury, so Bloodlust has nothing to convert — and Move Quick kites the follow-up. Bait the dart first. At 6 Undying Rage buys a window, but his shrooms punish sloppy dives.

edits.before: - Teemo Blinding Dart: matchup-defining — Blinds your crit-autos. Fight when down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Blinding Dart: a flat 7s at 680 range — the blind kills your autos, which kills your Fury, which leaves Bloodlust nothing to convert. That gap is the whole lane. - Undying Rage: 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Track Teemo's Blinding Dart: Blinds your crit-autos. Fight when down. When it is down — Crit him down.
edits.after: The blind starves you twice — no autos means no Fury, so Bloodlust has nothing to convert.

edits.before: Blinds your crit-autos. Fight when down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Blinding Dart is a flat 7s — bait it, then run the pattern inside that gap.

edits.before: That is Teemo's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Mocking Shout only slows him while he runs — and it cuts his Toxic Shot damage.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Mushrooms bounce off other mushrooms, so the far ones reach you too.

notes: The blind's real cost was stated nowhere: it removes your damage and your sustain in one cast, because no autos means no Fury and Bloodlust converts Fury. Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank, which makes it the most trackable cooldown in the matchup and worth naming. Move Quick's passive speed breaks when a champion or turret strikes him but the active sprint does not — I named the slot but did not write the split, since the page had no field short enough to carry it inside the band.
